storage_policy: Preserve original Unicode/NFC in research metadata; seeded game-facing form is Latin-1-compatible unless a documented Unicode opt-in is chosen.
normalisation: NFC at the whole-string boundary before validation and encoding; do not globally decompose supported Latin-1 characters.

contextual_exceptions.ȝ: The generic display mapping y is only a last-resort display approximation. A name-specific reviewed form may require g, gh or z instead; never use this lossy conversion as a canonical key.
contextual_exceptions.ə: The display fallback e is not a phonetic assertion. Retain the canonical source spelling separately.

algorithm: For unsupported scalars, use an approved explicit mapping when available.
Otherwise canonically decompose that scalar, remove nonspacing marks, then NFC-compose the remainder and encode if supported.
Flag unhandled printable characters in catalogue validation; do not silently introduce question marks into seeded names.
Use a fresh fallback buffer per encoder operation; do not reuse one mutable buffer across independently active encoders.
engineering_notes: The existing fallback has a shared mutable buffer and no usable surrogate-pair replacement. Specify behaviour for unsupported supplementary characters and test it separately.
MaxCharCount must cover the longest replacement actually emitted.
Keep ANSI/MXP protocol handling separate from text transliteration; do not strip protocol bytes or apply name validation to control sequences.
Prefer a precise authored Latin-1 display form over automated linguistic transliteration.
Lossy display forms must not be used to merge people, profile elements or canonical entity keys.
